audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was scored as a Lucian stage in both layers while whys[4] says the fight is a coin-flip ('hence even'), and the packet chart calls stage 5 'Skill'.
audit.why: Fury of the Sands (120/100/80s) grants bonus Health, Attack Range, armour and MR while dealing percent-max-health damage, so a topped-off Nasus answers The Culling. Even is the honest verdict.
audit.corrected: phases[4].side and win[4] -> 'Skill'. Stages 6 and 7 already read Nasus per the mirror (nasus__lucian) and are left untouched.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why described The Culling in a vacuum and never named the enemy's level-6 spike.
audit.why: The level-6 stage is decided by Fury of the Sands, not by The Culling — the resist and percent-health swing is what turns the all-in.
audit.corrected: Name Fury of the Sands at Level 6 and give the bail condition.

audit.whatIsWrong: The pages tracked 'Wither' with no cooldown and never mentioned that Siphoning Strike is an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: Wither is 15/14/13/12/11s at 700 range and slows Move and Attack Speed over time; Siphoning Strike is a 255-range auto reset, so the damage arrives on the wind-up rather than on a visible cast. Both change when you step in.
audit.corrected: Give Wither's real cooldown and tie the step-up to its downtime; treat his auto wind-up as the retreat cue.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warns that raw resistances and HP are the wrong buy into Fury of the Sands.
audit.why: Fury of the Sands carries the percentHealth flag — stacking health is punished, and he gains resists himself during the storm.
audit.corrected: Not written into report[8]: the itemization line is already at its length ceiling with the anti-heal instruction (Soul Eater lifesteal), which is the higher-value item advice. Recorded here instead.

audit.why: Both packet suspectNames are false positives: 'Ardent Blaze' is Lucian's real W name, and the 'With Q-' hit in whys[2] is a fragment of prose, not an ability name.

edits.before: The Culling adds lane-clear and execute chip — use it through walls on recalls and low-HP escapes.
edits.after: The Culling kills a low-stack Nasus; Fury of the Sands adds resists and percent-HP burn — bail if he ults.

edits.before: Keep the pressure rolling but track Wither — your lead is HP-bar bullying, not all-in math, until items arrive.
edits.after: Keep bullying, but Wither is up every 15/14/13/12/11s — step in only when it is spent, never onto his Q reset.

edits.before: Nasus spends Wither early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Wither is 15s at rank 1 — step up in its downtime and dash before it lands.

edits.before: That’s Nasus’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Siphoning Strike is an auto reset — the wind-up is your cue to go, not his cast.

notes: Mirror nasus__lucian had already moved stages 6 and 7 to Nasus; those rows were left exactly as the mirror set them. The only chart change is stage 5 to the neutral 'Skill', which is mirror-safe because the token is identical from both sides. Packet defect 'Lucian wins only 46.14% but the chart gives Lucian 4/7' is now 3/7 Lucian, 1 Skill, 2 Nasus (plus stage 5 Skill = 3 Lucian, 2 Skill, 2 Nasus). Whether the early stages should be de-rated further is a judgement the mirror already declined to make.
